final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral framework for Friday signature: 75% auto RVC with 16% labor-value content phased over three years (60/8→70/12→75/16), independent labor panel with quarterly audits and automatic 30-day enforcement, Chapter 19 binational preserved for all investment/goods disputes, dairy supply management protected from future panel review, and a 16-year term. Canada's initial resistance collapsed under combined U.S.-Mexico-Congress pressure, with USTR and Mexico repeatedly threatening bilateral fallback that Congress warned would fail ratification.
minority_objections: Canada initially demanded full Chapter 19 retention AND dairy protection without any carve-out, but was isolated and forced to accept the labor-panel carve compromise
key_conflicts: Canada vs. USTR/Mexico/Congress over Chapter 19 scope (full binational vs. labor-carved)
Dairy/Ag vs. Canada over supply management access (resolved by explicit text protecting Canadian regime)
Auto/Supply-chain vs. enforcement design over year-one grace period vs. immediate penalties
key_concessions: Canada accepted independent labor panel carve-out from Chapter 19 (initially a red line)
U.S./Congress accepted dairy supply management protection in agreement text (initially demanded opening)
USTR accepted 30-day retool window before suspension clock starts (initially implied immediate penalty)
Mexico accepted Chapter 19 preservation for investment disputes (initially pushed full elimination)
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 binational for investment/goods disputes (held)
USTR/Congress: Independent labor panel with automatic enforcement (held)
Mexico: 75% RVC and 16% labor-value content non-negotiable (held)
Congress: Trilateral deal required for ratification (held)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Actual audit capacity and inspector deployment logistics (Labor raised but never fully resolved)
Supplier readiness for year-one 60% RVC compliance despite 30-day window
Political durability of dairy protection language in future U.S. administrations
Mexican enforcement institutional capacity beyond panel design
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional ratification vote timing and margin (repeatedly invoked as constraint but never quantified)
Canadian Cabinet/Parliament approval of Chapter 19 carve-out compromise
Actual supplier capex commitment rates post-signature
Labor panel inspector recruitment and deployment timeline
Year-one compliance rates and whether 30-day window proves sufficient
uncertainty_notes: While the framework converged, three operational details remained unresolved: (1) exact audit frequency beyond 'quarterly' (how many plants, what triggers), (2) inspector team composition and deployment authority, (3) whether the 30-day retool window applies per-supplier or per-violation. Congress and USTR asserted ratification certainty but never specified vote counts or timing. Canada's final signature was implied but not explicitly confirmed in transcript.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC and 16% labor-value content were non-negotiable (Mexico R1, USTR R1); drove three-year phase-in compromise (USTR R3) and 30-day retool window (Congress R7) — shaped entire enforcement architecture
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Unannounced audits, 90-day suspension, quarterly inspections, eight-inspector team, and automatic 30-day warning mechanism were all demanded by Labor/Congress as ratification prerequisites (R2-R7) and drove independent panel carve-out from Chapter 19
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy supply management was Canada's stated red line (R2, R5, R6); U.S. Dairy/Congress initially demanded opening (R2-R6); final compromise was explicit text protecting regime from future panel review (R7) — nearly blocked deal
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada refused to sign without Chapter 19 binational for investment/goods (R2, R5, R6, R7); drove labor-panel carve-out compromise and explicit text preserving binational review (Congress R7) — was make-or-break issue
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Sunset raised by Supply-chain (R4, R5) as investment-uncertainty problem; USTR locked 16-year term (R5) which resolved concern — discussed but did not drive negotiation direction, term length was USTR decision not a negotiated compromise
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress repeatedly invoked ratification failure as veto threat (R1, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7); drove trilateral requirement, labor enforcement design, and Friday deadline — was primary stated constraint on all parties
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto/Supply-chain raised retool costs, capex timing, phase-in needs, and year-one compliance concerns (R2, R3, R4, R6, R7); influenced 30-day retool window but did not change core RVC/labor numbers — acknowledged and accommodated, not decisive
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico and USTR repeatedly threatened bilateral signature without Canada (R1, R3, R4, R5, R6); Congress warned bilateral would fail ratification (R1, R3); this bilateral-threat/ratification-veto dynamic forced Canada's concessions on Chapter 19 and drove Friday deadline
